note: Curated capability map. Capability rows are recovered from docs/ROADMAP.md, which is the only document that groups requirement identifiers by product area, and reconciled against shipped code. CAP-CLOUD has no ROADMAP row: the hosted control plane shipped without an entry, which is recorded as DOC-D-011 in docs/observatory/meta/coverage-and-contradictions.md.

status_vocabulary.implemented: Enforced by shipped code in this repository and reachable by a user of a self-hosted install.
status_vocabulary.gated: Shipped in this repository but withheld from the public surface by a build or provisioning gate.
status_vocabulary.planned: Recorded as intent only. No enforcing code in this repository.

capabilities.title: Foundation and toolchain
capabilities.summary: The monorepo, environment schema, emulators, and continuous integration that every other capability is built on.

capabilities.title: Identity and access
capabilities.summary: Verified sign-in, a default-deny request gate, and an owner allow-list, with a loopback-only development shortcut.

capabilities.title: The typed career graph
capabilities.summary: Typed nodes and typed edges validated per type, written transactionally, versioned by revision, and soft-deleted rather than destroyed.

capabilities.title: Capture
capabilities.summary: A keyboard capture line and schema-driven entity forms that create valid, linked, undoable records.

capabilities.title: Organize, trash, and retention
capabilities.summary: Saved views, revision history, a thirty-day trash with restore, and a purge that makes the retention promise real.

capabilities.title: Search and wayfinding
capabilities.summary: Unified full-text search, a composable filter grammar, and a fuzzy quick-switcher, all scoped to the active data space.

capabilities.title: Relationship intelligence
capabilities.summary: Typed relationship editing, one-tap interaction logging, Hawkes tie strength, reconnect ordering, and explainable contact ranking with warm-introduction paths.

capabilities.title: Explore
capabilities.summary: The Life map, the Chronograph timeline, and the Atlas of places, each with a keyboard and list equivalent and URL-backed state.

capabilities.title: Staged import
capabilities.summary: External sources staged into reviewable batches that are idempotent, committable, rollbackable, and attributable to their origin.

capabilities.title: Identity integrity
capabilities.summary: A duplicate candidate queue scored on shared evidence, an evidence-led merge, learned aliases, merge history, and a conflict-aware undo.

capabilities.title: Resume evidence and tailoring
capabilities.summary: Atoms and variants scored against a parsed job description, selected to a one-page budget, escaped, rendered to LaTeX, compiled, and checked for coverage.

capabilities.title: Career tracking
capabilities.summary: Applications as graph records with pipeline overview, linked posting, target, resume, company, referrer, and interview context.

capabilities.title: Export and restore
capabilities.summary: A self-describing JSONL and Markdown bundle with checksums and a manifest, and a restore path that validates before it writes.

capabilities.title: Operate and observe
capabilities.summary: Liveness and readiness probes, a health page, graceful shutdown, a storage adapter, an isolated compile service, and a secret store kept outside application data.

capabilities.title: Hosted workspace and billing control plane
capabilities.summary: Server-derived workspace scoping, idempotent workspace bootstrap, a server-owned plan catalog, signed provider webhooks with replay protection, and a lifecycle gate that keeps a locked workspace readable and exportable.
capabilities.note: Shipped in the repository and covered by integration tests, but not enabled for the public. The public build gate is VITE_PUBLIC_CLOUD_ENABLED and the server provisioning gate is separate. No hosted service is asserted to be operating.

capabilities.title: Cross-cutting platform behavior
capabilities.summary: The constraints that hold across every screen and endpoint: request correlation, error mapping, timezone correctness, authenticated transport, accessible overlays, shared contracts, and the performance rules that keep the graph read once.
